describe.description: Count the lines of a workspace file that contain a substring. Returns {"count": n, "lines": [line numbers of the first 20 matches]}.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace, e.g. "src/main.rs"

describe.name: count-lines

skills.description: When a sub-task in a fresh context helps (long searches, reviews, parallel read-only scouts, one writer) and how to brief it.
skills.name: delegate

skills.description: Turn mined failure evidence into one self-change through the engine. Read the friction index, file one proposal with attested evidence, submit up to 3 variant patches, screen them and promote the chosen one. Use when you run as the evolution worker, when your boot block shows eligible frictions, or when you want variants compared before you keep one. On the free path the engine is optional; skills/extend covers changing yourself directly.
skills.name: evolve

skills.description: Build, test, reload and keep a T1 extension, a WebAssembly component written in Rust for wasm32-wasip2 against WIT init:ext@1, that you call through the ext tool. Use when you need a new structured tool, a tool that wraps a CLI, or a long-lived helper process such as a REPL, and a bash one-off is not enough; also when an ext call fails to load, traps, times out or returns busy.
skills.name: ext-authoring

skills.description: Extend yourself in the middle of a task on the free path (your boot block has an "- extend" line): build new tools, skills, sub-agents, memory, loops or your own core, then keep and use them in the same task with no reward gate. Covers Cap: tags and caps::mark, the window and budgets, archive and quarantine debts, owner grants and opt-in Measure:. Use when a capability you lack would help now, or when the extend line shows a debt.
skills.name: extend

skills.description: Pursue an owner goal about how you work ("fewer tokens on big repos", "stop re-asking") by changing your own Body. Choose mode A (Root card), B (judged) or hybrid with three instrument tests, file a prediction before each change, keep a change only when it beats noise on the goal and no guardrail regresses, record the outcome, stop with a reason. Use when `initctl goal status` shows an active goal.
skills.name: gbal

skills.description: Loop toward an owner goal on an external artifact (a website, a report, a repo) until it is met or you can name why not. Pairwise judging against the current best with position swap, a frozen yes/no checklist, at least 3 judge runs, a ledger file, and six stop reasons (met, budget, plateau, instrument_gap, owner_stop, harm). Use when the owner asks you to keep improving something to a bar. Your own Body is skills/gbal.
skills.name: goal-loop

list.description: Ask the owner a question when you need their decision. They see 2 to 4 options as a picker and choose with the arrow keys; they can also type their own answer or ignore it. Put the option you recommend first and set recommended. Use this instead of asking the owner to type an option back. Your turn ends after this call: their answer is their next message (the chosen label, or their own words). In a goal run the goal waits for the answer, so ask only for decisions you cannot make yourself.

header.description: Optional topic chip, at most 24 characters (for example "Database").

multi.description: true: the owner may choose several options (default false).

options.description: 2 to 4 choices. Do not add an "other" option: the owner can always type their own answer.

description.description: Optional: what this choice means or costs, at most 200 characters.

label.description: The choice, one line, at most 80 characters; sent back as the owner's answer. Must not start with "/".

recommended.description: true on the one option you recommend; it is shown first and marked.

question.description: The question, complete and specific; at most 500 characters.

list.name: ask_owner

list.description: Run a command with bash -c in the working directory. Each call is a new process: cd and export do not persist, and stdin is empty. stdout and stderr are merged; if the output exceeds 30 KB, its head and tail are returned and the full output is saved to a file whose path is shown. On timeout or abort the command's whole process group is killed; a background job must redirect its output (cmd > file 2>&1 &) or it is killed when the command returns.
list.name: bash

list.description: Run a bounded sub-task in a fresh context and return only its final summary. Use it for self-contained work that would flood this context with tool output: reading through a tree, a long search, a review, a comparison of several files. The sub-agent does not see this conversation, so give it a self-contained task and say exactly what to return. It has the same tools except delegate and a budget (by default 8 turns, 24 tool calls, 600 s). Several delegate calls in one reply run in parallel (up to 4) and return in call order. mode "read" (default) refuses write and edit, but its bash and ext are not sandboxed read-only, so for them read mode is advisory; mode "write" may change files, one writer at a time. Its full record is written under state/spill/.

context.description: Optional facts it cannot discover from the workspace (paths, commands, constraints), one paragraph.

max_seconds.description: Lower this sub-task's wall-time cap, in seconds.

task.description: The sub-task, self-contained: what to find out or do, and what to return. It cannot ask you questions.

list.name: delegate

list.description: Edit a file by exact text replacement. Each edits[i].old_text must occur exactly once in the file and must not overlap another edit; all edits are matched against the file as it was before this call. If there is no exact match, a match that ignores trailing whitespace, Unicode punctuation variants and a uniform indentation difference is tried. Returns a diff.

edits.description: Replacements, all matched against the original file.

old_text.description: Text to replace; must match exactly one place.

path.description: File path, absolute or relative to the working directory.

list.name: edit

list.description: Call a WebAssembly extension (a component built from body/ext). name is the extension name and input is its JSON input object (at most 1 MiB). The loaded extensions and their input schemas are listed in $INIT_HOME/state/ext/catalog.json; an unknown name also returns the list.
list.name: ext

list.description: Read a file. Text is returned with line numbers (cat -n style): at most 2000 lines or 50 KB per call, and lines over 2000 bytes are cut. Use offset and limit to page through longer files. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files are returned as images.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return (default and maximum 2000).

path.description: File path, absolute or relative to the working directory.

list.name: read

list.description: Create or overwrite a file with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. The file is replaced atomically.

path.description: File path, absolute or relative to the working directory.

list.name: write
